title: Lena and the Witness
premise: Ivo Crane, the meticulous archivist of St. Aldhelm's Cathedral, is hired by a nervous stranger to prove that a murder has not yet happened — a crime foretold in a ledger hidden within the cathedral's locked crypt, tied to an inheritance dispute over the Vane estate. As Ivo decodes the cipher, she realizes the prophesied victim is her own estranged sister, and the client who hired her is the killer covering his tracks. Racing the opening of a wrongful-inheritance trial, Ivo must choose between legal justice and a private reckoning; in the end she exposes the conspiracy at the trial itself, saves her sister, and accepts that love — not duty — was the case she could never close.
about_author: Silas Blackwood is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing dead men's debts in English cathedral archives. They write mysteries about people who find murder filed neatly between baptisms and burials.

chapters.title: The Client Who Paid in Advance
chapters.summary: Ivo Crane's POV. A gray-eyed stranger arrives at the cathedral archive, pays triple for one task: prove a murder hasn't happened yet. He leaves no name, only a date three weeks out. Ivo, who never takes a case she can't close, accepts against instinct. Beat: unease disguised as professional curiosity.

chapters.title: A Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Searching the cathedral's donation ledgers for the client's reference number, she finds entries whose amounts encode letters — a cipher running through two centuries of bookkeeping. The final entry is dated the day of the promised murder. Beat: the thrill of the hunt curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. The cipher's key, she deduces, lies with the Vane family vault beneath the cathedral — sealed since 1911 by ecclesiastical order. Her petition to open it is denied by Dean Halloway, who seems afraid of something other than dust. Beat: first wall, first hint of institutional complicity.

chapters.title: Sister of the Accused
chapters.summary: Mara Crane's POV. Ivo's estranged sister Mara, executor of the contested Vane inheritance, prepares for trial as counsel for the estate. She hasn't spoken to Ivo in six years. A threatening note warns her to withdraw. Beat: pride and loneliness braided together.

chapters.title: What the Dead Man Paid For
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Decoded, the ledger names Edmund Vane — dead eleven years — and predicts his 'second death': the posthumous destruction of his will. The client's advance payment matches a sum in the ledger exactly. Ivo realizes she was hired by the murderer. Beat: betrayal, cold and clarifying.

chapters.title: The Gray-Eyed Man
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Tracing the payment through a solicitor's shell firm, Ivo identifies the client: Julian Ashe, the opposing counsel in Mara's trial. Confronting him would burn her invisibility; ignoring him dooms the will. Beat: the hunter realizing she is also bait.

chapters.title: Six Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara finds evidence someone has been inside her office — papers shifted, the will's safe copy disturbed. She suspects Ivo, the sister who once testified against their father. Beat: old wounds reopened, misdirected suspicion tightening the knot.

chapters.title: Halloway's Confession Half-Given
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo corners Dean Halloway, who admits the crypt holds more than bones: a sealed deposition from 1911, another forged will, another family ruined. The Church buried it then; someone means to bury it again now. Beat: history rhyming, dread deepening.

chapters.title: The Cipher Breaks
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Using the 1911 deposition's known text as a crib, Ivo cracks the full cipher. The ledger isn't a prophecy — it's a confession written across generations by the same hand: a forger's dynasty, and Ashe is its heir. Beat: revelation's vertigo.

chapters.title: An Offer of Silence
chapters.summary: Julian Ashe's POV. Ashe offers Ivo a fortune to return his payment and forget the case, revealing he knows she is Mara's sister — her invisibility was the point of hiring her. Beat: seduction of complicity, and its refusal forming.

chapters.title: The Trial Opens
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The inheritance trial begins. Ashe produces a 'newly discovered' codicil voiding Edmund Vane's will, its provenance immaculate. Mara smells forgery but can't prove it without the original — locked in the crypt. Beat: the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Breaking and Entering Holy Ground
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Out of lawful options, Ivo picks the crypt lock at night with the verger's stolen keys. Inside she finds the 1911 deposition and Edmund Vane's true will — but the crypt door grinds shut behind her. Beat: triumph inverted into trap.

chapters.title: Buried With the Evidence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Trapped in the dark among coffins, Ivo reads the will by matchlight: it names Mara sole heir and accuses the forgers by name. Someone knew she'd come. Beat: fear transmuting into fury; she memorizes every word before seeking the air vent.

chapters.title: The Sister Who Came Back
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Mara, tipped by an anonymous note in Ivo's handwriting, forces the crypt open and finds Ivo half-frozen beside the will. Six years of silence break in a single embrace. Beat: reconciliation paid for in near-tragedy.

chapters.title: Admissible
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The will is tainted by how they found it; the judge may exclude it. Mara argues chain-of-custody around Ashe's own break-in, buying time but not victory. Beat: hope on a technicality, fragile as glass.

chapters.title: The Verger's Tongue
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo traces who stole the verger's keys: Halloway's secretary, on Ashe's payroll since before the trial began. The rot reaches the dean himself, who chose silence over scandal decades ago. Beat: the institution's mask slipping entirely.

chapters.title: What Duty Demands
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Police involvement would expose Mara's break-in and sink the case. Ivo weighs law against justice and chooses the courtroom gambit: let Ashe believe he's won, then destroy him publicly. Beat: resolve hardened into strategy.

chapters.title: Closing Arguments
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Final day of trial. Mara calls a surprise witness — the elderly granddaughter of the 1911 forger, produced by Ivo — who identifies the cipher hand as her family's, and Ashe's training in it. Beat: the net closing, breath held.

chapters.title: The Murder That Hadn't Happened Yet
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ashe, cornered, moves to destroy the last ledger page during recess; Ivo has already swapped it. Confronted with the decoy and the real page in the judge's hands, he confesses in open court — the 'murder' was always the will's assassination. Beat: climax; justice outside the law, delivered inside it.

chapters.title: Sentencing the Living and the Dead
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. The will stands; Mara's clients inherit. Halloway resigns rather than face the 1911 reckoning, and the crypt is finally opened properly, its deposition read aloud. Beat: bittersweet vindication; institutions limp on, individuals made whole.

chapters.title: Two Sisters, One Archive
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Ivo declines a fee she no longer needs, returning Ashe's blood money to the court. She and Mara catalogue the Vane papers together, awkwardly, laughing for the first time in years. Beat: tenderness after ruin; love chosen over duty.

chapters.title: The Case She Couldn't Close
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, epilogue. Ivo files the case under a new heading in her private ledger: unsolved things of the heart. A new stranger climbs the archive stairs with an impossible request. She prides herself, still, on never taking a case she can't close — and smiles. Beat: quiet, wry peace; the door left open.
